answer: Each agent identity posts a 900-unit bond held for 50 epochs, registered against one hardware credential whose key cannot be copied to another machine. A sybil attacker locking N bonds must fund 900×N units and loses 100 percent of every slashed bond after a 5-epoch challenge window. Splitting identities multiplies that cost per fake key, and independent jurors sample the shared basalt, jetty, and willow attestations to slash duplicates.
